summary: At just 1.6 square miles, Artesia packs more than 10,000 people per square mile into a footprint smaller than many regional parks, making it one of the densest cities in Los Angeles County that almost nobody outside the area has heard of. The terrain is pancake-flat — classic LA Basin floor — with no ridgelines or ocean views, just a tight grid of commercial corridors and residential blocks bisected by the 91 Freeway and South Street. That freeway access is the practical trade: you're a bedroom community feeding jobs in Cerritos, Long Beach, and greater LA, not a standalone employment hub, so commute dependency is baked in. A median home price near $764,000 against a median household income around $97,700 yields a price-to-income ratio above 7.8 — aggressive even by Southern California standards, meaning purchasing requires substantial savings or equity from elsewhere, while median rent at $2,276 consumes roughly 28% of gross income. Pioneer Boulevard runs through town as a dense commercial strip loaded with restaurants, grocery shops, and gold-jewelry storefronts, giving Artesia a retail identity that punches well above its tiny acreage. With 9.5 hours of daily sunshine and average highs around 76°F, the climate is mild and consistent year-round, though green open space is scarce relative to the density. Artesia is essentially a hyper-compact commercial corridor with housing attached — the question is whether that compression reads as convenient or claustrophobic.
